  (Q_1 \times Q_2)\left[E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1} E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}\right]
  &= Q_1[E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1}] Q_2[E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}]
  \le 1
  \: .
\end{align*}
Let's now check the numeraire property.
Let $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2}$. Let $E^*_1 = E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1}$ and $E^*_2 = E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}$.
\begin{align*}
  (P_1 \times P_2)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_1 E^*_2} \right]
  &= P_1\left[\frac{1}{E_1^*}P_2\left[\frac{f}{E^*_2}\right] \right]
  \: .
\end{align*}
If we can show that $x \mapsto P_2\left[\frac{f(x, \cdot)}{E^*_2}\right]$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1}$, then we can apply the definition of the numeraire for $(P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1)$ to obtain

  &= P_1\left[\frac{1}{E_1^*}P_2\left[\frac{f}{E^*_2}\right] \right]
  \le 1
  \: .
\end{align*}

\label{def:condNumeraire}
  
Let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be a Markov kernel and $H \subseteq (\mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y})$ a set of Markov kernels.
